title: Sideways, Uneventful Monday
summary:
Sideways, Uneventful Monday 

             
             
            On occasion, we'll use the "summertime" adjective to characterize a Monday or Friday trading session during the summer months that may as well have been part of a 3-day weekend. A similar phenomenon can play out between mid November and the new year. Today would certainly be a candidate. In other words, trading momentum was sideways in a narrow range that largely fell inside the previous session's trading range. Volume and liquidity were low and there were no interesting reports or headlines that created any interesting reactions in the market.  A reasonably big drop in oil prices failed to inspire correlated bond buying, and the same could be said for a medium-large sell-off in the stock market. The latter is consistent with our recent warning that stocks would likely need to break below their early November lows before the bond market would care.

title: Correction to The Correction Over?
summary:
While we can certainly correlate the recent bond rally with uncertainty in the tech sector, it's also fair to say that yields were high enough to be on the lookout for a correction (so fair that it was a fixture in our commentary for most of September and early October). In other words, the tech stock slide could be viewed as the spark, but the fuel was already in place. The implication of viewing that rally as a correction is that the rally momentum is finite unless there's extraordinary levels of additional motivation. Instead, we got higher inflation reports and a supportive bounce in stocks. That provided a clear impetus for the correction to--well... correct. As of last Friday, that bearish correction showed early signs of running its course and this morning is offering a bit more confirmation. From here, bonds are as free as they've been in a while to flip a coin to choose the direction of the next move. 
  
 All that having been said, you're still more than welcome to view the bond market's fate as being tied to the risk that tech stocks fall back into their old ways from 2 weeks ago.

title: Two Signing Bonuses. One Six-Hour Drive.
summary: "This other offer is pretty tempting."A loan officer told me that while deciding between our company and two competitors. I appreciated the honesty. One company had offered him a sizable signing bonus. The other had a decent bonus on the table, too.We weren't offering one.Both companies had talked shop with him. They'd discussed compensation, held Zoom calls, and made their pitches. Neither had met him in person.I'd already met him a couple of times. I've always made a point of meeting someone face-to-face before hiring them. Maybe that's old-school, but I'm not comfortable asking somebody to make a major career move based entirely on a video call.

title: Kortas Expands FSBO.com Lead Strategy With Opendoor Deal
summary: NEXA Lending founder Mike Kortas is expanding his mortgage lead-generation strategy through a new partnership between FSBO.com and Opendoor, adding cash offers to a platform designed to connect loan officers with homeowners before they enter the traditional homebuying process.The agreement allows eligible FSBO.com sellers to request cash offers from Opendoor, which also operates its own mortgage lending business. But FSBO.com told NMP that the partnership will not send mortgage leads to Opendoor Home Loans.

title: Figure CEO Says AI Could Cut DSCR Loan Process to Days
summary: Figure Technology Solutions is aiming to cut the time it takes to process debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) loans from several weeks to days, using artificial intelligence to automate underwriting as it expands into investor lending following its acquisition of Kiavi.CEO Michael Tannenbaum told NMP that the company's new DSCR product will automate document reviews, property valuations, and portions of the title process, potentially allowing brokers to handle more loans without adding staff.

title: CFPB Moves Closer To Overhauling Mortgage Servicing Rules
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has sent a revised mortgage servicing rule to the White House for review, bringing the agency closer to finalizing changes that could reshape how servicers handle delinquent borrowers and foreclosure proceedings.

title: Mortgage Solutions Financial Shifts Originations To Fairway
summary: Mortgage Solutions Financial is moving its origination operations to Fairway Independent Mortgage Corp. effective Nov. 30, as its Colorado-based parent company winds down independent mortgage lending to focus on servicing.The transition will bring CEO Rob Clennan and MSF's sales team to Fairway, where they will continue originating loans under the Mortgage Solutions Financial brand. The division will also retain its own underwriters, processors, and closers.

title: Small Servicers Warn FASB Proposal Could Accelerate Industry Consolidation
summary: The Independent Community Bankers of America  (ICBA) is urging the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) to reconsider a proposed change to mortgage servicing rights valuations, warning that the new requirements could push smaller banks out of servicing and concentrate more of the business among the industry's largest players.

title: Fannie Mae's Rental Income Deadline Nears, With New Rules For Investor Loans
summary: Mortgage brokers working with real estate investors have two weeks to prepare for Fannie Mae's revised rental income requirements, which could affect how borrowers qualify for conventional mortgages when relying on recently acquired rental properties.The changes, announced in September, become mandatory for loan applications dated Dec. 1 or later. Fannie originally set a Nov. 1 deadline before extending implementation by one month.
